# Results — Study 522 (Percent Operating Accruals) on the real tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Signal: Hafzalla-Lundholm-Van
Winkle (2011) percent operating accruals = (Net Income − Operating Cash Flow) / |Net Income|
from annual 10-K facts (EDGAR `companyconcept`, data.sec.gov). Forward returns from yfinance
daily adjusted closes collapsed to calendar-year total returns. As-of **2026-06-26**.*

**Definition**:
- operating accruals = Net Income − Operating Cash Flow
- percent accruals = (Net Income − Operating Cash Flow) / |Net Income|
- HIGH percent accruals → earnings mostly non-cash → predicted LOW future returns

**Sort**: quintiles each fiscal year; hedge = **Q1 (low percent accruals) − Q5 (high)**
(long cash-backed, short accrual-heavy).
**Reporting lag**: fundamentals from fiscal year y → returns in calendar year y+1 (exactly
one execution lag, no look-ahead, no same-bar fills).
**Universe**: fixed 40-name large-cap **survivor** basket, all still trading in 2026.
**Window**: 17 hedge years (signal 2008–2024 → returns 2009–2025). The incomplete 2026
calendar year is excluded — no partial years in this stamped run.

**SURVIVORSHIP-BIAS WARNING**: the basket is a fixed set of large caps still trading in
2026. Firms that overstated earnings, collapsed, and were delisted — precisely the
high-accrual disasters the short leg wants — are absent. Every number below is an UPPER
BOUND on a live strategy.

## Quintile returns (percent accruals low → high, forward 1 year)

| Quintile | Mean return | Sharpe | HAC t-stat | Hit rate |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **Q1 (low PA — most cash-backed)** | **+16.3%/yr** | +1.16 | +7.28 | 88% |
| Q2 | +20.1%/yr | +1.32 | +7.44 | 100% |
| Q3 | +13.3%/yr | +1.28 | +7.02 | 88% |
| Q4 | +15.5%/yr | +1.13 | +5.83 | 82% |
| **Q5 (high PA — least cash-backed)** | **+13.7%/yr** | +0.96 | +4.81 | 76% |
| Equal-weight market | +15.7%/yr | +1.56 | +10.47 | 88% |

The sort is **not monotone**: Q2 (not Q1) is the best quintile, and Q1 barely separates
from Q5. The HLVW prediction (cash-backed quintile leads, accrual-heavy lags) does not hold
on this survivor panel.

## Long low-PA / short high-PA hedge (Q1 − Q5)

| Metric | Gross | Net (after costs) |
|---|--:|--:|
| Mean annual return | **+2.6%/yr** | **+1.9%/yr** |
| Sharpe ratio | +0.15 | +0.11 |
| HAC Newey-West t-stat | **+0.84** | +0.64 |
| Hit rate (positive years) | 47% (8/17) | 47% |
| n (years) | 17 | 17 |

The gross hedge t = **+0.84** is far below the desk's |t| ≥ 2 bar. After costs it falls
further. The hedge swings wildly year to year (−41.8% in 2023, +32.5% in 2022) — pure noise.

## Costs

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| One-way transaction cost | 10 bps × 2 legs × turnover |
| Mean annual long-leg turnover | 62% |
| Short-leg borrow | 50 bps/yr (full NAV on the short side) |
| Gross → Net hedge | +2.6%/yr → **+1.9%/yr** |

## Excess vs equal-weight market

| Arm | Excess return | HAC t-stat |
|---|--:|--:|
| Low-PA (Q1) | **+0.6%/yr** | **+0.29** |
| High-PA (Q5) | **−2.0%/yr** | **−1.06** |

Neither leg is significant. The long leg gives essentially zero excess; the short leg's
−2.0%/yr underperformance is the only directionally-correct effect, but at t = −1.06 it is
indistinguishable from noise.

## Label-shuffle placebo (1000 permutations)

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Real hedge HAC t | +0.84 |
| Null hedge t (mean ± std) | +0.11 ± 1.23 |
| **Placebo p (|t| ≥ |real t|)** | **0.460** |
| Placebo p seed-robustness (5 seeds) | 0.477, 0.517, 0.460, 0.433, 0.457 (mean 0.469) |

The real signal is statistically **indistinguishable from randomly shuffled labels**
(p ≈ 0.47, stable across seeds). There is no edge to speak of.

## Random-portfolio null (long-leg size, 500 draws/yr)

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Random excess mean | +0.12%/yr |
| Random excess std | 7.6%/yr |
| Low-PA portfolio beats random draw | **54%** of 500×17yr draws |

The low-PA portfolio is no better than a coin flip against same-size random baskets.

## Synthetic positive control (engine faithfulness — NOT a real-tape claim)

| Planted premium | Single-seed t (522) | Mean t over 20 seeds | Fraction \|t\| > 2 |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 0 (null) | +2.58 | **+0.02** | 0% |
| −5%/yr (high PA underperforms) | +13.03 | **+9.89** | 100% |

The engine is faithful: a null panel averages t ≈ 0 (0 false positives across 20 seeds),
while a planted −5%/yr percent-accruals premium lights the hedge up every time. Note the
single-seed null t = +2.58 — a textbook **lucky-seed** artefact; the desk rule of averaging
a Welch-style stat over ≥ 20 seeds correctly reports the truth (mean t = +0.02). This is a
power check only and is **never** cited to support the real-tape verdict.

## Verdict

On a fixed 40-name large-cap survivor basket, 2009–2025, the HLVW (2011) percent-operating-
accruals long-short hedge earns **+2.6%/yr gross (HAC t = +0.84)**, **+1.9%/yr net of
costs** — comfortably below the |t| ≥ 2 bar. The quintile sort is non-monotone (Q2 leads,
not Q1), the long leg's excess is +0.6%/yr (t = +0.29), and the only directionally-correct
piece (the short leg, −2.0%/yr) is itself insignificant (t = −1.06). A label-shuffle placebo
puts the real t at p ≈ 0.47 — **indistinguishable from random**, stable across seeds — and
the low-PA basket beats only 54% of same-size random draws.

The synthetic control proves the engine would detect a real percent-accruals premium
(mean t = +9.89 with a planted −5%/yr effect over 20 seeds); the real tape simply has none
to detect.

**Does scaling by earnings beat Sloan's asset-scaling (Study 231)?** No — not here. On the
*same kind* of survivor panel, Study 231's asset-scaled Sloan hedge reached HAC t = +2.73;
the HLVW percent-scaled version comes in at t = +0.84. HLVW's headline claim (percent
accruals sort *more* sharply) is **busted** on this large-cap survivor sample — consistent
with the literature that both accrual signals have decayed on liquid large caps post-2000
and survive mainly in small, illiquid names that this basket excludes.

- **Signal — NONE** (gross HAC t = +0.84, placebo p ≈ 0.47, non-monotone sort, beats only
  54% of random draws; even this is a survivorship-biased upper bound).
- **Tradability — MIRAGE** (annual rebalancing is operationally cheap, but there is no edge
  to harvest — net t = +0.64; a tradable wrapper around a non-signal).
- **Percent-scaling beats Sloan? — BUSTED** (t = +0.84 vs Study 231's +2.73 on a comparable
  survivor panel; HLVW's sharper-sort claim does not replicate on large-cap survivors).
